Risk Description: Inappropriate use of company owned assets may introduce malware or viruses into the network resulting in a breach or compromise of sensitive data.
If devices on the network do not have antivirus software installed, a virus could enter the network leading to a security incident or breach.

[Deactivate this risk if your organization is not pursuing the Availablity criteria as part of your SOC 2 audit. Delete these instructions and score the risk if it is.] A lack of (or ad hoc) capacity management and system monitoring practices can lead to system failures or delays that result in interruptions and diminishing trust in reliability of services.

Failure to adopt and test a business continuity plan can lead to an inability of the organization to efficiently and effectively resume operations or provide timely access to sensitive data. This may result in fines from enforcement agencies or litigation due to not meeting minimum security requirements.

If changes to systems, settings, or software are implemented without authorization, testing, and approval, vulnerabilities and errors can be introduced. This can result in a decrease in stakeholder trust in the integrity and/or availability of the system, settings, or software.
Active Controls: Change Management: Application/Software, Change Management: Infrastructure, Change Management Policy, Separation of Environments, Change Management: Emergency Process, Change Management: Separation of Duties, Change Management: Ticketing System

Risk Description: Non-compliance with laws and regulations can lead to fines or penalties and reputational damage, impacting customer trust in the integrity of the product and/or management.

[Deactivate this risk if your organization is not pursuing the Confidentiality criteria as part of your SOC 2 audit. Delete these instructions and score the risk if it is.]  Unprotected confidential information can result in unintentional destruction or distribution, or over-retention of confidential data.

Inadequate contractual agreements can lead to an inability to hold third parties accountable to basic security standards and requirements which can compound reputational damage and financial repercussions from a data breach.

If security control ownership is not defined then controls can go un-executed due to lack of oversight. This exposes the company to data breaches, security incidents, malfeasance, and criminal behavior which can erode internal and external trust in the organization.
If board or management involvement is lacking, this may lead to poor corporate oversight and decision-making.

If data is inappropriately accessed and/or disclosed by internal or external parties it will lead to regulatory ramifications, an impact on business reputation and stakeholder trust, and liability for damages.

A lack of data classification results in inappropriate access to data/systems and improper handling of the data based on the risk that data poses. This can lead to a data breach and the release of private or sensitive information and an erosion of customer trust.
Active Controls: Data Flow Diagram, Data Management Policy, Asset Inventory, Data Classification Policy, Data Retention/Deletion

Risk Description: Failure to encrypt sensitive or confidential data in transit can result in unauthorized access or modification of sensitive or confidential data, inappropropriate disclosure or theft of data, or fines from regulators and erode stakeholder trust in the organziation's data security practices.

Inadequate procedures for proper workstation and connected network device security may result in inconsistent security settings applied to devices, a data breach, unauthorized access to data, unauthorized devices connecting to the network, and inappropriate tampering of devices.

[Deactivate this risk if your organization does not host production servers on-site. Delete these instructions and score the risk if they are on site.]  Without adequate safeguards to protect servers from environmental hazards such as fire and water, data can be lost or corrupted.
Informal inbound and outbound communication channels and ad hoc, vague, and confusing communications diminish stakeholder trust in the organizations' credibility.
If fraud is not considered when reviewing revenue and expenditures in financial practices or when hiring, the company can experience financial loss or legal action.
The lack of standard personnel management practices leads to ineffective use of personnel resources and low employee morale and accountability.
Inadequate or no procedures in place to address or track security incidents can allow adversaries to continue to access restricted data or allow security incidents to go unremediated.
Active Controls: Incident Response: Employee Responsibility, Incident Response: Testing, Incident Response: Process

Risk Description: Without a formal intrusion detection system, bad actors may gain undetected access to the system.

A lack of information security oversight can result in a weakened and vulnerable control environment, leading stakeholders to lose trust in the organization's ability to main their commitments to data security, availability, confidentiality, and integrity.
Inappropriate access to backend systems can result in a data breach or security incident by allowing bad actors to bypass established network security procedures.
A lack of robust password management may lead to disclosure of password or login information, fines from regulators, breach of data, and unauthorized access or modifications of data.
Active Controls: Password Requirements, User Authentication, Logical Access Policy

Risk Description: If infrastructure (server operating systems, server hardware) is not regularly patched, known vulnerabilities can be found and exploited.

[Deactivate this risk if your organization is fully remote. Delete these instructions and score the risk if you have a physical office.] Lack of building/facility security controls leads to loss and/or theft of data or assets.

Without effective corporate communication, staff may be unable to meet the organization's objectives for information security and data privacy. This can impact stakeholder trust in the organization's ability to meet contractual obligations, relevant regulations, or compliance initiatives.

[Deactivate this risk if your organization handles no personally identifiable information. Delete these instructions and score the risk if PII is handled within your organization. If your organization is only pursuing the Security criteria as part of your SOC 2 audit, specific privacy controls are not required even if your organization does handle personally identifiable information.] If user data protections have not been defined or are not secured with relevant security criteria, it can result in reputational damage, fines, and breach of contracts, severely impacting stakeholder trust.
A lack of restrictions to sensitive or privileged assets can lead to inappropriate or unauthorized changes resulting in a breach of sensitive or confidential data.
Active Controls: Separation of Duties: IT Operations, Administrator Access

Risk Description: [Deactivate this risk if your organization is not pursuing the Processing Integrity criteria as part of your SOC 2 audit. Delete these instructions and score the risk if it is.]  Lack of processes and procedures to ensure that data flows into and out of systems and processes to ensure the quality of data, may lead to incomplete, inaccurate, or untimely services.

A lack of a clearly defined reporting structure leads to competing directions and confusion about meeting company objectives. A lack of oversight can allow negligence or criminal activity to go unnoticed and increase the impact of a security incident or breach, as well as diminish employee trust in the integrity of organization leadership.
Active Controls: Job Descriptions, Organizational Chart, Management Oversight

Risk Description: Inadequate training on cybersecurity practices can result in a disruption of business processes of information system functionality, a data breach, unauthorized access to the network or facility, installation of unauthorized software or applications, a social engineering attack, and misuse of company assets.
Active Controls: Incident Response: Employee Responsibility, Security Training

Risk Description: If a system to control access to source code does not exist or is not maintained, it may result in unauthorized or inappropriate changes to code.
Active Controls: Separation of Duties: Developers, Change Management: Application/Software

Risk Description: Inadequate monitoring of network systems can allow exploitation of unpatched systems, a breach of data, a denial of service attack, or unauthorized access to the network.

If a regular review of configuration settings and changes to the system (Cloud service configurations and policies, server configurations, and access controls) is not regularly conducted, vulnerabilities can result from improperly configured systems, hardware, and data storage.

If user data protections have not been defined or are not secured with relevant security criteria, it can result in reputational damage, fines, and breach of contracts, severely impacting stakeholder trust.
Active Controls: Logical Access Policy, User Access Review, Termination of Access, Provisioning, User Authentication

Risk Description: [Deactivate this risk if your organization handles no personally identifiable information. Delete these instructions and score the risk if PII is handled within your organization. If your organization is only pursuing the Security criteria as part of your SOC 2 audit, specific privacy controls are not required even if your organization does handle personally identifiable information.] If the organization collects more than the minimum amount of data needed to provide its service or has not defined what data needs to be provided for the correct use of its services, it may be in breach of contract or in contradiction to laws and regulations, resulting in a lack of trust by end-users.

The lack of a program to ensure that vendors and contractors comply with organizational policies and requirements can lead to vendor malfeasance, negligence, or a supply chain attack. This can result in a data breach or security incident, which can negatively impact stakeholder trust.
Active Controls: Vendor Risk Register, Third Party SOC2, Vendor Review, Vendor Management Policy, Vendor Due Diligence

Risk Description: Without a vulnerability assessment (penetration testing and/or vulnerability scanning), network and application security vulnerabilities are not identified for remediation, leaving the system open to attack. A lack of consistent vulnerability scanning and follow-up to close vulnerabilities may introduce network and/or application vulnerabilities that will not be remediated. This will increase the likelihood of a data breach or security incident and damage customer trust in the organization.
